text.p: Entergy Corp's current series of regulatory filings mark the beginning of the complex process of transitioning to competition, Jerry Jackson, executive vice president - external affairs told analysts Thursday.
The proposals being made to regulators in Mississippi, Louisiana, Arkansas and Texas would "permit Entergy to recover all of its prudently incurred costs," he said.
Jackson said the filings are designed to accomplish two major objectives.
"First, they provide a mechanism to accelerate recovery of all pre-1996 investment in Waterford 3, Arkansas Nuclear One and River Bend generating plants.
"Second, the filings propose a non-bypassable universal service charge that would prevent cost shifting from one customer group to another."
The filings provide for a rate freeze in certain jurisdictions and a performance-based rate plan in Texas during the transition period, Jackson said.
"We will accelerate the amortization of the investment in the nuclear generating plants regulated by Arkansas, Louisiana, and Texas public service commissions over a seven-year timeframe," he said.
"The accelerated depreciation will be funded by a rate freeze, where appropriate, sales and revenue growth, further cost reductions and certain depreciation transfers," Jackson said.
"One objective is that the decrease in core business net income during the transition period would be more than offset by expected increases in net income from our diversified growth businesses."
